linkedin.title: Most people feel overwhelmed by the news because they are reading the wrong things for them.
linkedin.body:
It is not that there is too much information in the world. It is that the information we consume is rarely curated for our specific interests or needs. When you open a standard news app, you are often fed a firehose of headlines designed to trigger a reaction rather than build understanding.

True information literacy is not about reading everything. It is about reading the right things. Personalization should not mean creating a bubble where you only hear what you agree with. It should mean filtering out the noise so you can focus on the topics that actually impact your work, your life, and your curiosity.

We built Headlinne to change the dynamic. By using AI to learn what you actually care about, we help you cut through the clutter. You get a briefing that respects your time and intelligence, helping you stay informed without the usual digital fatigue.

instagram.caption:
A major Microsoft outage briefly took down key communication tools like Outlook and Teams, leaving users worldwide unable to

access their accounts.

The disruption was significant enough to affect critical public infrastructure, including schools and medical services.

Microsoft has since confirmed that the underlying issue is resolved and services are coming back online. They have issued an apology for the inconvenience caused by the downtime.

story_card.caption:
Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent and Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick are clashing over Nvidia chip exports to China.

The dispute centers on whether the Commerce Department failed to block shipments to a firm with suspicious links. This public disagreement exposes significant friction within the current administration regarding how strictly to enforce tech trade bans. It raises questions about how the U.S. will manage sensitive technology exports moving forward.
